title: Beyond tariffs: The US–Turkey trade relationship needs a bigger bargain
gist: US tariffs have evolved from protectionism into a tool that conditions market access on partners' contributions to US economic security, leaving Turkey with a 12.5 percent forced-labor Section 301 rate, Section 232 steel tariffs and potential up-to-100 percent penalties under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The author proposes a structured US-Turkey economic security bargain trading tariff relief for market access, supply-chain safeguards and Turkey's industrial and geographic reach, to advance the stalled $100 billion trade goal.

insights.claim: Washington now uses tariffs not only to protect domestic industry but to push partners to invest in the US, align with US regulatory and economic-security priorities and build secure supply chains, so market access increasingly depends on contribution to US industrial goals.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Trade exposure for any country is now a function of geopolitical alignment and investment pledges, not just trade balances.
insights.quote: The result is a trade system in which market access increasingly depends on a country’s contribution to US industrial and economic-security goals.
